children: Regional banking company Independent Bank

reported Q3 2026 results topping the market’s revenue expectations, with sales up 7.5% year on year to $261.9 million. Its non-GAAP profit of $1.90 per share was 2.9% above analysts’ consensus estimates.
Independent Bank (INDB) Q3 2026 Highlights:
Revenue:
$261.9 million vs analyst estimates of $260.2 million (7.5% year-on-year growth, 0.7% beat)
Adjusted EPS:
$1.90 vs analyst estimates of $1.85 (2.9% beat)
Market Capitalization:
$3.62 billion
StockStory’s Take

Independent Bank’s third quarter results were met with a strong market response, reflecting the company’s ability to sustain loan and deposit growth in a highly competitive environment. Management credited broad-based strength across commercial and consumer lending, robust deposit inflows, and stable net interest margins as key contributors to outperformance. CEO Jeff Tengel emphasized that “the best use of our capital is to build deep, profitable customer relationships and not grow our balance sheet at thin, risk-adjusted spreads,” highlighting prudent growth as a central theme.

Looking forward, Independent Bank’s outlook is shaped by ongoing deposit competition, evolving credit conditions in office and commercial real estate, and the anticipated benefits of upcoming technology investments. CFO Mark Ruggiero stated the company expects continued expansion in loan yields and a focus on “holding the line on expenses,” with priority placed on technology enhancements and disciplined cost management. Management also pointed to resolution of select office-related non-performing loans and the core system upgrade as critical milestones for operational efficiency and long-term profitability.
Key Insights from Management’s Remarks

Management attributed third quarter performance to resilient loan pipelines, disciplined pricing across lending and deposits, and proactive capital deployment, while addressing the impact of higher rates on customer behavior and credit quality.
Loan growth across segments:

The company achieved notable growth in commercial and industrial (C&I), commercial real estate (CRE), home equity, and residential mortgage loans. Tengel highlighted that “C&I loans rose by $61 million, or a healthy 5% on an annualized basis,” driven by new client acquisition and improved origination activity.
Deposit inflows and cost discipline:

Deposits increased over $630 million on average, with non-time deposits playing a significant role. Management noted the cost of deposits remains industry-leading, despite a competitive landscape. Ruggiero stated, “Our deposit franchise continued to differentiate itself…with 5.4% annualized growth.”
Maintained net interest margin stability:

The adjusted net interest margin (NIM) held steady, benefiting from favorable repricing of loans and securities. The company’s approach to balancing asset yields against rising deposit costs contributed to margin resilience, with Ruggiero noting an improved mix of earning assets.
Credit quality and office exposure:

Credit performance remained consistent with historical averages, though the company proactively recognized reserves on select office loans that moved to non-performing status. Management detailed a $6.5 million reserve for a local office loan and ongoing efforts to resolve two large non-performing office credits, with Ruggiero emphasizing, “The loss has been taken for the most part, so it should not result in much more needed provision levels.”
Expense and technology management:

Non-interest expenses were managed tightly, aided by lower director equity grant expenses and a delay of the core system conversion to February. Management expects this upgrade to enhance operational efficiency and product capabilities, with minimal incremental cost due to the postponement.
Drivers of Future Performance

Management expects loan and deposit growth to continue, but sees headwinds from higher rates, credit normalization, and the timing of technology investments affecting both revenue and expense trajectories.
Loan and deposit growth outlook:

The company anticipates mid-single digit growth in C&I loans and low single-digit increases in CRE and construction, supported by a healthy pipeline but tempered by customer caution due to higher rates. Home equity demand is expected to remain strong, though mortgage activity is likely to stay subdued.
Margin and expense dynamics:

Ruggiero forecasted modest net interest income growth and a net interest margin “slightly north of 3.9%” if rates remain stable, but acknowledged potential pressure from deposit costs if the Federal Reserve raises rates again. Management plans to maintain expense discipline, with targeted investment in technology and AI only partially offset by savings from operational consolidation.
Credit and reserve management:

While credit quality remains stable, management is closely monitoring office and life sciences exposures. Proactive reserving and ongoing dialogue with sponsors are expected to limit future provision spikes, but persistent high rates or real estate valuation declines could necessitate further adjustments.
Catalysts in Upcoming Quarters

Looking ahead, our analysts will monitor (1) the resolution pace of non-performing office and life sciences loans and associated reserve releases, (2) the impact and execution of the core systems upgrade scheduled for early next year, and (3) continued momentum in loan and deposit growth despite competitive and rate pressures. Progress in adopting AI-enabled internal tools and realizing operational efficiencies from headquarters consolidation will also be tracked as key drivers of future profitability.
Independent Bank currently trades at $79.62, up from $77.08 just before the earnings. At this price, is it a buy or sell?
